title: Bounded modification genus ascends through separable finite extensions
statement: Let $R\hookrightarrow S$ be a finite injective local homomorphism of commutative normal Nagata local domains of Krull dimension $2$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume that the induced extension $\operatorname{Frac}(S)/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], where $\operatorname{Frac}$ denotes the field of fractions of a domain. If reduction to rational singularities is possible for $R$, then it is possible for $S$ [def-per-rational-surface-singularity].

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}S$. By [def-per-rational-surface-singularity], choose $B\geq0$ bounding $\operatorname{length}_R H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for every normal modification of $R$. Apply [lem-per-integral-trace-dual-lattice] to the given finite injective map and its separable fraction-field extension. Fix its basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ and nonzero $d\in R$ once and for all. These choices depend on $R\hookrightarrow S$, not on any modification.

source.place: Tag 0AXL, first paragraph and boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Let $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ be any normal modification. By [lem-per-normalized-generically-finite-domination] obtain normal modifications $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}S$, a proper birational $S$-morphism $h:Y\to Y_0$, and a compatible finite morphism $\pi:Y\to X$. Apply [lem-per-modification-h1-exact-sequence] with $A=S$ (Noetherian, being Nagata), the normal modification $Y_0$ in the role of $X$, $Y$ in the role of $X'$ and $g=h$; its hypotheses hold since both are integral and proper over $\operatorname{Spec}S$ inducing isomorphisms of function fields, $Y_0$ is normal, and $h$ is an $S$-morphism. Its first arrow is an injective $S$-linear map $h^*:H^1(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})\hookrightarrow H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ of Zariski cohomology. Thus a uniform length bound for the latter gives the same bound for the original arbitrary $Y_0$.

source.place: Tag 0AXL, second paragraph; Tag 0AXF for the domination reduction.

proof.text: Use [lem-per-integral-trace-dual-lattice] on this finite map between normal models. It gives $0\to\pi_*\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{\Phi}\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to Q\to0$ with $dQ=0$. Finiteness implies affineness by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; the structure sheaf is quasi-coherent (on an affine it is the module associated to its coordinate ring), so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] identifies $H^1(X,\pi_*\mathcal O_Y)$ with $H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ as $R$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], the abelian category of module sheaves has enough injectives; global sections is left exact since kernels are computed sectionwise. The module cohomology convention is [pqf-def-cohomology]. The long exact derived-functor sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact], applied to global sections of sheaves of modules, therefore gives an exact segment $H^0(X,Q)\to M\xrightarrow{\alpha}H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)^{\oplus n}$, where $M=H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. Here finite direct sums commute with this cohomology: take the finite direct sum of injective resolutions, which remains an injective resolution since a finite sum is a finite product, and apply global sections termwise. Since $dQ=0$, linearity of the connecting homomorphism gives $d\ker\alpha=0$. By [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] these module-cohomology groups are canonically isomorphic to the Zariski cohomology groups of [def-per-rational-surface-singularity], naturally in the sheaf; naturality for the multiplication endomorphisms by elements of $R$ (on $\mathcal O_X$) and of $S$ (on $\mathcal O_Y$) makes these isomorphisms $R$- resp. $S$-linear. So $M$, $\alpha$ and the bound $B$ of Step 1 may be read in Zariski cohomology, as Steps 2, 4 and 5 do.

source.place: Tag 0AXL, third paragraph, exact cohomology segment.

proof.text: The image of $d$ in $S$ is nonzero by injectivity of $R\to S$. Apply [lem-per-normal-surface-modification-torsion-bound] with $(A,a)=(S,d)$: there is $C\geq0$ independent of $Y$ with $\operatorname{length}_S M[d]\leq C$. Write $k_R=R/\mathfrak m_R$, $k_S=S/\mathfrak m_S$ and $e=[k_S:k_R]$. This integer is finite: finite $R$-module generators of $S$ descend to a spanning set for its quotient $k_S$ over $k_R$; locality makes $\mathfrak m_R$ act by zero. The singleton maximal ideal of $S$ contracts to $\mathfrak m_R$, as required for [lem-exc-semilocal-restriction-length]. Apply it to the finite-length $S$-module $M[d]$. As $S$ is already local, localization at its maximal ideal changes neither the ring nor the module, and it gives $\operatorname{length}_R M[d]=e\operatorname{length}_S M[d]\leq eC$.

source.place: Tag 0AXL, last two sentences; Tag 0AXJ and algebra Tag 02M0 for restriction of scalars.

proof.text: By Step 3, $\ker\alpha\subseteq M[d]$, so its $R$-length is at most $eC$. The image of $\alpha$ has $R$-length at most $nB$, since it is a submodule of $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)^{\oplus n}$. Consequently $\operatorname{length}_R M\leq eC+nB$. These elementary length inequalities follow directly from [def-weil-pbc-module-length]: chains in submodules remain chains in the ambient module; chains in a quotient lift by inverse image; in a short exact sequence a strict inclusion in a chain in the middle must induce a strict inclusion either in its intersection with the kernel or in its image in the quotient, giving the sum bound. Applying this repeatedly also bounds the length of a finite direct sum by the sum of its lengths. Every strict chain of $S$-submodules is a strict chain of $R$-submodules, so $\operatorname{length}_S M\leq\operatorname{length}_R M$. The injection of Step 2 gives $\operatorname{length}_S H^1(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})\leq eC+nB$. This bound is independent of $Y_0$, proving the required reduction property by [def-per-rational-surface-singularity].

source.place: Tag 0AXL, final boundedness inference with its module-length argument written out.
